Definition: Pre-execution enforcement point that denies write/edit attempts before mutation when containment, instruction-root, symlink, mode, or permission policy fails.

Synonyms: project root;project-root containment;active project or working root
Definition: The active runtime containment root that bounds ordinary writes; treated as equivalent to the decomposition phrase 'project root' until canonical naming is chosen.
The release/change containment root that ordinary project execution must not mutate (K-ROOT-2).
A required exact content match or equivalent precondition for edit-style operations before mutation; matcher and diff strategy remain TBD.
Initial policy that rejects symlink targets and symlink path segments for writes (K-PATH-3).
Denial of filesystem operations outside the active project or working root before mutation.
Rule that denials from policy, path containment, hook, governance, SDK deny rule, or human gate override any allow.
Behavior in which hook failures result in denial (no mutation) for write/edit and related actions.
Requirement that Chirality MCP write tools pass through the same permission, hook, path, redaction, and event logging policy as SDK built-ins.
Safe diff/summary, permission/runtime event, and source metadata evidence recorded for allowed and denied write attempts.
Permission mode that cannot perform write/edit operations.
Permission mode that allows governed writes only after permission and hook gates pass.
SDK tool allowlist that must not be treated as a sufficient restriction or safety boundary for write/edit capability (K-PERM-3).
Gated Chirality MCP tool requiring explicit mutation classification before exposure.
Chirality MCP write/gated tool in the current source inventory.
Chirality MCP write/gated tool (dependency writer) in the current source inventory.
Reference source state (REF-006) marking docs/PRD.md as warning-qualified until reconciled or a governed hash-bypass record is accepted.
Hook phase that records successful write provenance, diff/summary, and safe metadata after mutation.
Write/edit performed atomically where practical only after permission and hook gates pass; not a substitute for pre-execution checks.
